correctness.rationale: An affine-invariant Löwner certificate says any candidate enclosing ellipsoid is unique volume-minimizing if its touching generators admit a probability distribution whose normalized mean is zero and covariance I/d. Small spike: uniform cube vertices normalized by sqrt d. Intermediate phase: center 0, axial a, transverse a sqrt((d-1)/(a^2-1)); give apex weight p=(a^2-d)/(d(a^2-1)) and cube weight q=(d-1)a^2/(d(a^2-1)) with first-sign mean -(a^2-d)/(a(d-1)); all are probabilities precisely between thresholds and give isotropy. Large spike: center (a-d)/(d+1), axial d(a+1)/(d+1), transverse d/sqrt(d+1); put 1/(d+1) apex and d/(d+1) on negative-facet vertices. Direct symbolic mean/covariance, contact, containment, and both logarithmic volume second-derivative jumps verified. Thus global optimality over arbitrary ellipsoids is certified, not only axial candidate comparison. The positive cube facet has strictly smaller normalized radius when center>0, but its vertices remain extreme.
residual_risks: Axial single spike and Euclidean metric only; no general exterior direction or multi-spike extension.
